content:
Jennie starts with 60 letters needing stamps and an unknown number of letters already stamped. She puts stamps on one-third of the letters needing stamps:  
\(\frac{1}{3} \times 60 = 20\) letters.  

These 20 letters are moved from the "needing stamps" pile to the "already stamped" pile. After this, the "already stamped" pile contains 30 letters.  

Let \(x\) be the original number of letters in the "already stamped" pile. Then:  
\(x + 20 = 30\)  
\(x = 10\)  

So, there were 10 letters in the already-stamped pile when Jennie began.

Answer: 10
